questions.q: Before choosing a cloud provider or sizing any VM for Harrow Peak Outfitters, what does this lesson do first?
options: Deploy the cheapest available VM size and adjust later if it's too small
Skip requirements gathering since the old server's specs are good enough to copy
Pick AWS by default because it's the most widely used cloud provider
Write down the business's actual requirements -- uptime window, data residency, budget -- with the Operations Manager
questions.explain: Requirements gathering comes first: uptime window, data residency, and budget are business constraints every later technical decision has to satisfy.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose Azure for Harrow Peak Outfitters rather than splitting the workload across Azure and AWS?
options: AWS does not support virtual networks or security groups
Splitting workloads across two clouds is required for every deployment
Azure is always the cheaper option regardless of the workload
The company already runs Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, and a two-person IT function can't absorb the overhead of a second cloud
questions.explain: The provider choice is answered honestly for this specific workload -- existing Entra ID investment and a small IT team -- not split down the middle.

questions.q: How is the Standard_D2s_v5 app VM size decided?
options: By pulling real CPU and memory utilization off the old physical server and sizing against actual observed usage
By guessing based on how many employees the company has
By matching whatever size a different company used for an unrelated project
By picking the largest VM size available in the budget
questions.explain: Sizing comes from real numbers pulled off the existing server, not a guess padded for an imaginary peak.

questions.q: What is the correct deployment order for the network layer in this lesson?
options: Storage account first, since it has no network dependencies
VNet, then subnets, then NSGs, then a connectivity check -- all before any compute or storage exists
NSGs first, then subnets, then the VNet last
Compute first, then a VNet is added around it afterward
questions.explain: Chapter 2's network-first order applies directly: VNet, subnets, NSGs, and a verified connectivity check, before compute or storage.

questions.q: Why does data-subnet-nsg allow inbound traffic on port 1433 only from app-subnet's address range, instead of from the whole VNet or the internet?
options: It doesn't matter which source range is used as long as the port number is correct
Because Azure requires every NSG rule to use the broadest possible source range
Because port 1433 cannot be restricted to a specific subnet
To scope the rule to exactly what that subnet needs -- least-privilege, correct the first time, not opened wide and tightened later
questions.explain: Scoping the rule to app-subnet's range only is the least-privilege approach -- the database is never directly reachable from the internet or the rest of the VNet.
